answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The meadow multiplier is published, charged in wander, and tundra lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1718 identities would post 3326 proofs and burn roughly 31 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
